_doc: #624 — this app's RUNTIME ARTIFACT declared as a fleet lib, so the 400 MB glibc rootfs #618 moved out of the APK is a named, versioned member of the constellation instead of an anonymous release asset. Nothing about the artifact is restated here: `declared_in` + `at` POINT at the one #618 declaration (rootfs/rootfs.json::artifact), and data/regen.sh resolves the identity, the asset names and the urls from there. This file exists only to say WHO the artifact is to the fleet — the module name every other identity is derived from, per #474's one-declaration rule.
_doc_not_in_build_json: Deliberately its own file rather than a key in build.json. ac_cloud-nix-on-droid/build.json IS one of its artifact's identity_files, so adding a fleet key there would re-address a 370 MB asset and make every phone refetch it for a declaration-only change. The sibling keeps the same shape so the two are read by one scan.
_doc_module: The ONE name. id = lib-{module}, label = cloud-lib-{module} (#474, the same rule regen.sh applies to every lib APK). Not written out twice.
_doc_kind: NOT `app` and NOT `lib`: there is no APK and no package id here, so this entry is emitted into constellation-fleet.json's `catalogue`, never its `apps`. Fleet.parse reads only `apps`, so the updater, both auto-update workers and every install path are structurally incapable of being handed this row — a 437 MB installable APK is not merely discouraged, it cannot be constructed. The Constellation page draws catalogue rows from the same declared group as everything else.
what: The glibc root filesystem this terminal enters through proot: claude, goose, hermes, agy, node, fish. Fetched once from the release beside the APK, sha256-gated against the digest baked into assets/, extracted on first shell and never refetched while the digest matches.
